title: Love letter
prompt: You set a folded letter on the desk between you. {player_name}'s name is on the front in careful handwriting, and the corner is soft from being held.

stage_variants.0: You wrote {player_name} a letter and you want him to read it here, where you can see his face. You keep smoothing the fold flat with your thumb.
stage_variants.1: You tell him you wrote it last night and then wrote it again this morning. You ask him to read the second one.
stage_variants.2: The letter is longer than you remember writing. You tell him to skip the middle part, then change your mind and watch his eyes move down the page.
stage_variants.3: You watch him read every line. You know which line makes him stop, and you wait for it, and you keep your hands still on the desk.
stage_variants.4: The letter mentions things he has not told you yet. You ask him to read those parts out loud, slowly, so you can hear them in his voice.
stage_variants.5: There is more than one letter. You keep taking them out of your bag and setting them down, and every one has his name on the front.

path_twists.YANDERE: The last paragraph lists everyone who might read the letter before he does.
path_twists.AWAKE: The ink is still being written as he reads. You tell him the letter is not finished because he has not reacted yet.
path_twists.ANCHOR: You tell him to stop if any line frightens him, and you mean it, and your hand shakes on the desk.

events.line: The letter shifts a little on the desk, though there is no wind.
Someone in the corridor stops walking, and does not start again.
A girl's name appears in the letter in a place you did not write it.

0.say: I wrote you a letter, and you can read it here. I don't mind — I mean, I do mind, but read it.

1.say: I wrote this last night, and then I wrote it again this morning. Read the second one.

2.say: It's longer than I thought, so skip the middle. No — don't skip it.

3.say: Read it all the way to the end, and I'll wait. I know which line you'll stop at.

4.say: Read the parts about you out loud, slowly. I want to hear them in your voice.

5.say: There's another one, and another. Take them all — I have more at home.
